newsitem.title: ITALY: U.N. chief makes plea for aid for Zaire refugees.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief makes plea for aid for Zaire refugees.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali made an impassioned plea on Wednesday for immediate help for one million refugees in eastern Zaire, saying they faced "certain death" if nothing was done.

"The international community must come to the aid of the refugees in Zaire. We need everyone to help... This is an all-out emergency and every day counts," he said in a speech to the opening session of the World Food Summit in Rome.

Boutros-Ghali said on Tuesday that Canada had offered to lead a multinational force to secure food aid and passage for the refugees, scattered by four weeks of fighting in eastern Zaire. He said he believed the U.N. Security Council would give its mandate to the force in the next few days.
"At the very moment this summit is taking place, over a million starving, frightened refugees are wandering helpless in the mountains and forests of eastern Zaire," Boutros-Ghali said.

"From this platform, in this Eternal City, I make a solemn appeal to peoples and to states to take part, all of them, in the collective action we will undertake in the Great Lakes region," Boutros-Ghali told the summit.
"It is by our ability to take charge of this tragedy in a collective, concerted fashion that we will give a real meaning to human solidarity," he said to loud applause.
